chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The sorcerer of the Muslims is killed, and the sorcerer of the disbelievers is not killed.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and why is the sorcerer of the disbelievers not killed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because disbelief is greater than sorcery, and because sorcery and polytheism are paired.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the sorcerer of the disbelievers not executed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential principle of 'priority of the greater sin' (tarjih al-awzan), where the disbelieving sorcerer is exempted from the hadd penalty for sorcery because his inherent disbelief (kufr) is considered more severe than the act of magic itself. Scholars note that since sorcery is intrinsically linked to shirk, the disbeliever's status already covers the penalty, whereas the Muslim sorcerer requires specific execution for the distinct crime of magic. This ruling highlights the nuanced hierarchy of sins in Shia fiqh, distinguishing between the penalty for a specific act and the overarching state of disbelief.
